newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Mexico upped, Chile cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Mexico upped, Chile cut.

text.p: -- Lehman Brothers said on Monday it had cut its recommendation for Chile to underweight from overweight in its model portfolio of Latin American stocks.
-- Analysts Maryam Mansoury and Daryl Collins also raised Mexico to overweight from neutral in the portfolio. Other countries' positions remained unchanged.

-- "We are taking a more aggressive stance in our Latin American portfolio. We are increasing our positions to an overweight in Mexico at the expense of Chile, where we recommend an underweight position relative to the IFC benchmark," they wrote.
-- "... Our preferred sectors in Chile are telecom and electric utilities while in Mexico our bias is toward financials and cyclicals."

-- They added, "Chile's market performance is lagging the region's because of its lower risk return profile, while markets in economies at earlier stages of their reform process should continue to outperform. This essentially means that the scope for multiple expansion and growth will remain highest in countries where reforms continue to advance, bringing down overall country risk and unleashing secular growth."
